source_text: Καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐνενηκοστοῦ πέμπτου ψαλμοῦ τῶν διὰ Δαυῒδ λεχθέντων λόγων λέξεις βραχείας ἀφείλοντο ταύτας· ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου. Εἰρημένου γὰρ τοῦ λόγου· Εἴπατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν· Ὁ κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου, ἀφῆκαν· Εἴπατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν· Ὁ κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν . Ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἔθνεσι περὶ οὐδενὸς ὡς θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου ἐλέχθη ποτὲ ἀπὸ τῶν τοῦ γένους ὑμῶν ἀνθρώπων ὅτι ἐβασίλευσεν, ἀλλ᾿ ἢ περὶ τούτου μόνου τοῦ σταυρωθέντος. ὃν καὶ σεσῶσθαι ἀναστάντα ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ ψαλμῷ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἄγιον λέγει. μηνύον ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ὅμοιος τοῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν θεοῖς· ἐκεῖνα γὰρ εἴδωλά ἐστι δαιμονίων . Ἀλλ᾿ ὅπως τὸ λεγόμενον νοήσητε, τὸν πάντα ψαλμὸν ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν. Ἔστι δὲ οὗτος· Ἄισατε τῷ κυρίῳ ᾆσμκ καινόν, ᾄσατε τῷ κυρίῳ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ. Ἄισατε τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ εὐλογῄσατε τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ· εὐαγγελίζεσθε ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας τὸ σωτήριον αὐτοῦ. Ἀναγγείλατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς λαοῖς τὰ θαυμάσια αὐτοῦ· ὅτι μέγας κύριος καὶ αἰνετὸς σφόδρα, φοβερός ἐστιν ὑπὲρ πάντας τοὺς θεούς· ὅτι πάντες οἱ θεοὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν δαιμόνια. ὁ δὲ κύριος τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἐποίησεν. Ἐξομολόγησις καὶ ὡραιότης ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ. ἁγιωσύνη καὶ μεγαλοπρέπεια ἐν τῷ ἁγιάσματι αὐτοῦ. Ἐνέγκατε τῷ κυρίῳ, αἱ πατριαὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν, ἐνέγκατε τῷ κυρίῳ δόξαν καὶ τιμήν, ἐνέγκατε τῷ κυρίῳ δόξαν ἐν ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ. Αἴρετε θυσίας καὶ εἰσπορεύεσθε εἰς τὰς αὐλάς αὐτοῦ, προσκυνήσατε τῷ κυρίῳ ἐν αὐλῇ ἁγίᾳ αὐτοῦ. Σαλευθήτω ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ. Εἴπατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν· Ὁ κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου. Καὶ γὰρ κατώρθωσε τὴν οἰκουμένην. ἥτις οὐ σαλευθήσεται· κρινεῖ λαοὺς ἐν εὐθύτητι. Εὐφραινέσθωσαν οἱ οὐρανοί καὶ ἀγαλλιάσθω ἡ γῆ, σαλευθήσεται ἡ θάλασσα καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. Χαρήσεται τὰ πεδία καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς, ἀγαλλιάσονται πάντα τὰ ξύλα τοῦ δρυμοῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου κυρίου. ὅτι ἔρχεται, ὅτι ἔρχεται κρῖναι τὴν γῆν. Κρινεῖ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ λαοὺς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ αὐτοῦ . Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Εἰ μέν. ὡς ἔφης. εἶπε, παρέγραψάν τι ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν οἱ ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ. θεὸς δύναται ἐπίστασθαι· ἀπίστῳ δὲ ἔοικε τὸ τοιοῦτον. Ναί. ἔφην, ἀπίστῳ ἔοικε· φοβερώτερον γάρ ἐστι τῆς μοσχοποιΐας, ἣν ἐποίησαν ἐπὶ γῆς μάννα πεπλησμένοι, καὶ τοῦ τὰ τέκνα θύειν τοῖς δαιμονίοις. ἢ τοῦ αὐτοὺς τοὺς προφήτας ἀνῃρηκέναι. Ἀλλὰ δή. ἔφην. μοι νομίζεσθε μηδὲ ἀκηκοέναι ἃς εἶπον περικεκοφέναι αὐτοὺς γραφάς. Ὑπὲρ αὐταρκείας γὰρ αἱ τοσαῦται προανιστορημέναι εἰσὶν εἰς ἀπόδειξιν τῶν ζητηθέντων μετὰ τῶν λεχθήσεσθαι μελλόντων παρ᾿ ὑμῖν παραπεφυλαγμένων.
pass_a_gloss: And from the ninety-fifth psalm of the words spoken through David short phrases were removed these; from the wood. For the phrase having been spoken: Say in the nations: The Lord reigns from the wood, they removed: Say in the nations: The Lord reigns. And in the nations concerning no one as God and Lord was ever spoken by the people of your race that He reigns, except concerning this one alone who was crucified. Whom also the Holy Spirit says in the same psalm to have been saved, having risen. Indicating that He is not like the gods of the nations; for those are idols of demons. But so that you may understand what is being said, I will recite the entire psalm to you. And it is this: Sing to the Lord a new song, sing to the Lord all the earth. Sing to the Lord and bless His name; proclaim His salvation from day to day. Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples. For the Lord is great and worthy of praise, feared above all gods; for all the gods of the nations are demons. But the Lord made the heavens. Confession and beauty are before Him. Holiness and majesty are in His sanctuary. Bring to the Lord, O families of the nations, bring to the Lord glory and honor, bring to the Lord glory in His name. Take up sacrifices and come into His courts, worship the Lord in His holy court. Let all the earth tremble before Him. Say in the nations: The Lord reigns from the wood. For He has triumphed over the world, which will not be shaken; He will judge the peoples with uprightness. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad, let the sea and its fullness be shaken. The fields will be joyful and all that is in them, all the trees of the forest will rejoice before the Lord. For He is coming, for He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with His truth. And Trypho said: If, as you said, the rulers of the people have written something down from the scriptures, God is able to know; but to an unbeliever it seems implausible. Yes, I said, it seems implausible to an unbeliever; for it is more frightening than the idol-making, which they made on earth when they were full of manna, and than their sacrificing children to demons. Or than their killing the prophets. But now, I said, I think you have not even heard what I said, that they have cut out scriptures. For the many prophecies that have been mentioned before are sufficient to demonstrate the things being sought, along with the things that will be said and are being reserved to be said among you.

bible_refs.note: Say in the nations: The Lord reigns from the wood

pass_b_english: The ninety-fifth psalm, which was spoken through David, originally included a phrase that has been removed - a phrase that declared, 'The Lord reigns from the wood' (Psalm 96:10). What remains is the statement, 'The Lord reigns,' but the original phrase specified that God's reign began 'from the wood,' a reference to the cross. This is a unique claim, as no other god or lord in the nations has ever been said to reign in this way, except for the one who was crucified. The Holy Spirit, in the same psalm, affirms that this crucified Lord has been saved and has risen. This distinction highlights the difference between the Lord and the gods of the nations, which are merely idols of demons. To help clarify this point, I'd like to recite the entire psalm for you. It begins, 'Sing to the Lord a new song, sing to the Lord, all the earth.' The psalm continues, 'Sing to the Lord and bless His name; proclaim His salvation from day to day.' It also declares, 'Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples.' The reason for this declaration is that 'the Lord is great and worthy of praise, feared above all gods,' and this is because 'all the gods of the nations are demons.' In contrast, 'the Lord made the heavens,' and 'confession and beauty are before Him.' The psalm also states that 'holiness and majesty are in His sanctuary.' It invites the nations to 'bring to the Lord glory and honor, bring to the Lord glory in His name.' The psalm encourages worship, saying, 'Take up sacrifices and come into His courts, worship the Lord in His holy court.' And it concludes with a call to reverence, saying, 'Let all the earth tremble before Him.' The original phrase, 'The Lord reigns from the wood,' is a testament to God's triumph over the world, which will not be shaken. The Lord will judge the peoples with uprightness, and 'the heavens will rejoice and the earth be glad.' Even 'the sea and its fullness will be shaken,' and 'the fields will be joyful and all that is in them.' The natural world will respond to the Lord's coming, for 'He is coming to judge the earth,' and 'He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with His truth.' Trypho responded to this by saying that if the rulers of the people had indeed removed parts of the scriptures, God would be aware of it, but to an unbeliever, this seems implausible. I agreed that it might seem implausible to an unbeliever, but I pointed out that this action is more disturbing than the idolatry that the people had previously practiced, or their sacrifice of children to demons, or even their killing of the prophets. I expressed my concern that Trypho might not have even heard the prophecies I mentioned earlier, which provide sufficient evidence for the points I'm making, along with the additional points that I will discuss later.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the specific argument regarding the removal of the phrase 'from the wood' (ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου) and the subsequent recitation of the psalm. Pass A is a faithful literal translation, and Pass B is a faithful paraphrase. Scripture citations (Psalm 96:10) are correctly identified and applied to the relevant clauses.
